flawed_step: Choosing a maximum-degree vertex need not be compatible with any minimum vertex cover; arbitrary tie-breaking can force a suboptimal result.
counterexample: Let G be the path 1-2-3-4-5. Initially vertices 2, 3, and 4 all have maximum degree 2, so choosing 3 is legal. Deleting its incident edges leaves the disjoint edges 1-2 and 4-5. The algorithm must then choose one endpoint of each, for example 1 and 4, and returns {3,1,4}, of size 3. But {2,4} is a vertex cover of size 2, and no size-1 cover exists because edges 1-2 and 4-5 are disjoint. Thus the greedy output is not minimum.
assessment_summary: A legal execution on the five-vertex path returns three vertices although the minimum vertex-cover size is two.
